channel.description: Recent content in AI Agents on David Twizer's Site

item.title: llms.txt Is the Cheapest RAG You'll Ever Ship
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: My site’s chat agent answers with exact deep links to my posts - no search tool, no vector database. It reads /llms.txt at prompt time, and the whole ‘retrieval pipeline’ is one HTTP GET.

item.title: Get iOS Push Notifications When Your Agent Finishes (or Fails)
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: Wire an xpander agent’s success/error webhook into hark.ryan.ceo and your phone buzzes the moment a long-running agent task finishes - no polling, no forgotten tabs.

item.title: Two API Calls to Put an AI Agent on a Static Site
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: The “Chat with my AI” button is a real xpander agent - created with one API call, streamed with another, and dropped onto a static site behind a tiny key-holding Worker.

item.title: Do You Also Feel Cheated?
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: Instead of full delegation, we are literally working harder, not smarter.

item.title: The Next Productivity Paradox
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: AI agents only create durable productivity when they remove humans from being the integration layer between systems.

item.title: AI as the Micromanager?
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: It might be the most useful AI layer: watching the mess, extracting the work, and telling you what needs to happen next.

item.title: Why Your Organization Needs Agent Infrastructure, Not More Agents
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: The gap between “we have 5 agents” and “we have 500 agents” is not filled by buying more products. It is filled by building the foundation.

item.title: We're Not the Only Ones Building Agent Infrastructure. Here's the Difference.
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: An external vertical agent is not an internal agent. A platform that wraps your code and takes over the runtime is not really infrastructure.

item.title: The API Contract Without the Server
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: How AI agents change the traditional API development model: skip the server layer and let agents work directly with API contracts.

item.title: Build a Production-Ready Autonomous Expense Agent
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: Upload an invoice and the agent reads it, classifies it, renames it, files it into the right Google Drive folder, and keeps an audit trail: the parts that break in production, solved.

item.title: Introducing Slack-Native AI Agents
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: Deploy custom AI agents to Slack in minutes. They respond to mentions, keep memory across threads, and work like real coworkers inside the tools you already use.

item.title: Most AI Agents Are Just Fancy Chatbots
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: Autonomy without control is chaos. We don’t ship chaos. We ship infrastructure.

item.title: An Agent That Closes the Troubleshooting Loop
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: Automating the entire troubleshooting loop across Datadog logs and GitHub Actions. No tickets, no waiting.

item.title: How xpander.ai Embraces the Model Context Protocol in Practice: An Engineering Deep-Dive
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: The architecture, the gritty engineering challenges (from SSE streaming to multi-tenant security), and how we wove MCP into a production agent platform.

item.title: The Year AI Will Start Building and Managing Other AI Agents
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: When you have a genie in a bottle granting you three wishes, clever thinkers will ask the genie for another genie.

item.title: Announcing Agent Graph System: 4x Better Multi-Step Tool Use
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: An agent built with Agentic Interfaces and Agent Graph System hit a 98% success rate on multi-step tasks, versus 24% for GPT-4o alone, and did it 38% faster with 31.5% fewer tokens.

item.title: From Manual to Autonomous: Revolutionize Business Tasks In-House
item.author: David Twizer
item.description: How enterprises can build and deploy AI agents in-house: autonomous digital workers that automate complex tasks while keeping full control over data, security, and cost.
